issues.legal_issue: Credible eyewitness and injured-witness evidence, despite minor omissions and discrepancies, can sustain a finding that the accused inflicted fatal injuries.
material_facts: A witness who was the deceased’s brother testified that he saw the assault from an adjacent field.
The deceased’s son and other witnesses who were injured in the incident testified about the assault and corroborated the account of the eyewitness.
The omission of a detail about one weapon from the initial complaint was attributed to the witness’s shock and did not undermine his credibility.
The courts found that the discrepancies did not affect the core prosecution account, and the defence claim of political rivalry was not substantiated.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge to the prosecution evidence and upheld the concurrent finding that the appellants inflicted the fatal injuries.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered the eyewitness account alongside corroborating testimony from injured witnesses, whose evidence is entitled to great weight and requires a convincing ground to discard. Minor omissions and discrepancies that do not undermine the core account do not render the evidence unreliable.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.credible_eyewitness_account: A witness who had an opportunity to observe the incident gave an account the court found credible.
predicates.injured_witnesses_corroborate: Witnesses injured in the incident gave testimony corroborating the eyewitness account.
predicates.discrepancies_do_not_undermine_core_acco: The omissions and discrepancies in the evidence did not undermine the core account of the incident.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal presents a credible eyewitness account corroborated by injured witnesses, and discrepancies do not undermine the core account, the finding that the accused inflicted the fatal injuries is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A homicide committed without premeditation during a sudden fight in the heat of passion, without undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct, falls within the sudden-fight exception and is not murder.
material_facts: The incident arose when a bullock cart entered land whose occupants objected to its passage, followed by a verbal altercation and a sudden fight.
The occupants were proceeding to agricultural work, and the agricultural implements used in the assault were ordinary tools they could normally carry for that work.
The deceased sustained two incised injuries, and the evidence did not establish that the appellants took undue advantage or acted cruelly or unusually.
The Court found that the homicide occurred without premeditation in a sudden fight.
issues.conclusion: The Court applied Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC, altered the conviction from Section 302/34 IPC to Section 304 Part I IPC, and imposed a ten-year term of imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: Under Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC, culpable homicide is not murder when it is committed without premeditation in a sudden fight, in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and without the offender taking undue advantage or acting cruelly or unusually. All those conditions must be established; the fight must involve the person killed. The Court relied on Sridhar Bhuyan v. State of Orissa (2004) 11 SCC 395 for these principles and altered the conviction to Section 304 Part I IPC.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction and no_premeditation and sudden_fight and heat_of_passion and fight_involved_person_killed and not undue_advantage and not cruel_or_unusual_conduct

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal against a conviction for murder.
predicates.no_premeditation: The killing was not planned or preceded by a determination to fight.
predicates.sudden_fight: A fight arose suddenly between the participants.
predicates.heat_of_passion: The participants acted while passion from the sudden quarrel clouded their reason, without time for it to cool.
predicates.fight_involved_person_killed: The person killed was involved in the fight.
predicates.undue_advantage: The offender took an unfair advantage during the fight.
predicates.cruel_or_unusual_conduct: The offender acted cruelly or in an unusual manner during the fight.

issues.definition: In an appeal against a murder conviction, if the killing was unplanned and occurred in a sudden, heated fight involving the deceased, without unfair advantage or cruel or unusual conduct, the conviction is reduced to culpable homicide.
